#### 1.  The intersecting circles and the existence of the points \(A,B\)

The centres are  

\[
M=(0,0),\qquad N=(d,0),\qquad d>0,
\]

and the radii satisfy \(0<r<R\).  
The equations of the circles are  

\[
\Omega:\;x^{2}+y^{2}=r^{2},\qquad 
\Gamma:\;(x-d)^{2}+y^{2}=R^{2}.
\]

Subtracting the two equations gives the abscissa of the intersection points:

\[
x_{0}= \frac{r^{2}-R^{2}+d^{2}}{2d}.
\tag{1}
\]

Substituting \(x_{0}\) into \(\Omega\) yields  

\[
y_{0}^{2}=r^{2}-x_{0}^{2}.
\tag{2}
\]

Because the circles intersect in two distinct points we have  

\[
|R-r|<d<R+r .
\tag{3}
\]
